messages:
olivia: FYI — Acme reports their free-trial/promo credits landed on a sandbox org instead of their main org. They can’t spin up prod capacity until we move them.

olivia: Customer details: org names `acme-prod` (org_ABC123) and `acme-sandbox` (org_DEF456). Promo code `TRIAL2026` redeemed on 2026-02-28 and shows under acme-sandbox. They used GitHub SSO + later invited corporate SSO which looks like created a second org.

jules: thanks — tagging billing & infra. @samir can you confirm if this is a simple credits transfer or something we need to merge? Any quick repro steps?

samir: I can take a look. Quick check: from the admin UI go to /admin/orgs/ORG_ID/billing -> Credits. For a repro I logged into staging admin and searched by promo `TRIAL2026` and saw an allocation tied to org_DEF456 (sandbox).

samir: two possible fixes: 1) transfer credits from org_DEF456 -> org_ABC123 (preferred), or 2) merge orgs if accounts are duplicates and customer wants a single org id. Transfers are safer.

olivia: customer prefers transfer only. They explicitly asked NOT to merge.

kevin: heads up — when transferring, watch for concurrent promo redemptions. There’s a race where the promo service re-applies on sign-in if org metadata mismatches. Best: perform a reverse allocation + new allocation in a single DB transaction, and clear the promo redemption record on the source org.

samir: plan: run dry-run, then apply. Dry-run script: 
```
# dry-run: shows what will change
python admin_tools/credits_transfer.py --from org_DEF456 --to org_ABC123 --amount 10000 --dry-run
```
Will produce a delta file for review.

samir: can olivia confirm the exact amount to move? Customer said their trial shows $150 credit in the UI.

olivia: confirmed with customer — move 150 USD equivalent (system shows 150000 tokens/units).

billing-bot: [AUTO] Billing ledger snapshot created: ledger_snapshot_2026-03-01T09:12:33Z for org_DEF456.

samir: running dry-run now, attaching output. (attached snippet in thread)

samir: dry-run result: will create one negative allocation on org_DEF456 (-150) and one positive allocation on org_ABC123 (+150). No other promos affected.

kevin: good. After transfer, clear the promo redemption entry: `DELETE FROM promo_redemptions WHERE org_id = 'org_DEF456' AND code='TRIAL2026' LIMIT 1;` then re-issue a redemption record to org_ABC123 if necessary. Coordinate with me so I can watch logs for any background job that might re-run.

jules: please run during maintenance window? Customer wants it ASAP but we should do it during low-traffic. Samir, propose time.

samir: can run at 2026-03-01 14:00 UTC — will be quick (<5m). I'll post status updates.

samir: RUN: executed transfer at 2026-03-01 14:03 UTC. Commands used: 
```
python admin_tools/credits_transfer.py --from org_DEF456 --to org_ABC123 --amount 150 --apply --trace-id xfer-1802-01
# then
psql -c "BEGIN; UPDATE credits SET amount = amount - 150 WHERE org_id='org_DEF456'; INSERT INTO credits(org_id,amount,reason,created_by) VALUES('org_ABC123',150,'promo-transfer', 'samir'); DELETE FROM promo_redemptions WHERE org_id='org_DEF456' AND code='TRIAL2026' LIMIT 1; COMMIT;"
```

billing-bot: [AUTO] CreditTransferEvent recorded: xfer-1802-01, from=org_DEF456, to=org_ABC123, amount=150, status=SUCCESS

samir: verified UI: acme-prod (org_ABC123) now shows +150 in Billing -> Credits. acme-sandbox shows zero. No invoices were affected.

kevin: I monitored background workers; no promo reapplication observed. All logs clean.

jules: great work — olivia please notify customer and confirm they can provision. Also log this as a manual intervention in the account history.

olivia: messaged customer; they confirmed they can provision new instances and see credits in prod. They said thanks. Closing the loop. :tada:

samir: will put a short postmortem note into the billing runbook about duplicate SSO flows creating shadow orgs and a safe transfer playbook.

jules: adding this to the onboarding checklist: when corporate SSO is enabled, check for prior GH orgs and migrate promo redemptions.

olivia: closing thread — resolved.
